.qc-cache/hireops-2026-10-01-handoff-audit/task/instruction.md; tests/app_context.md; tests/gates/{render,constraints}/{judge.toml,prompt.md}; tests/scored/{functional,polish,visual}/prompt.md; tests/scoring.toml; tests/test.sh gate invocation lines
evidence: The actual frozen workbook Quality Checks!D30 and skill quality-checks.md:124 require auth AND server-backing legs in each scored dimension when relevant. The stale internal-sheet cross-origin exclusion is superseded by the public row and current public-network policy. HireOps explicitly requires backend persistence (task/instruction.md:1,9). The real gates are sound in source: render/judge.toml:23 pairs invalid and valid sign-in and rejects static pictures; constraints/judge.toml:23-26 requires successful UI requisition+offer creation and independent empty Auditor-context retrieval of the exact saved values, and excludes no-op/browser-only/static-seed responses. Both are binary all_pass; test.sh:213-222 evaluates these before the scored suite. However each scored gate lacks an explicit server-backing leg: functional/prompt.md:9 requires a saved record and readback but does not make that readback independent of browser storage; polish/prompt.md:6 only requires operational content with a usable saved record; visual/prompt.md:6 only requires an operational populated workspace, and :8 restricts review to read-only screens. All three require sign-in and zero blank/static shells, and none requires same-origin. Those words do not establish backend operation in these separate judge contexts. The template also lacks a backing probe in its scored gate text; the authoritative workbook requirement remains unmet and task-specific prompts may correct it. Current raw evidence hashes were verified: gate-witness/results.json=fd8410bc91102874ef98edfdbacf19f7853687956e076acc684d36c565d9ec75, mcp/results.json=c0a3672dfb069b54a930a07dd2b16a7582c097082cba544980666647da71513a, configured-inspection/results.json=6bf9aa47913875f44e0c4b16c35169eaa2d42a6d491ce59fc4898c414cb6facc. The configured-inspection tests_sha256 entries all match frozen tests. Scripted gate witness shows golden and dead-approval variant satisfy the basic storage gate, while no-op-create fails despite HTTP200. MCP evidence demonstrates available independent-context UI readback. These support the real gate and tool feasibility, not execution of every scored in-dimension backing gate; no configured-judge score or runtime reproduction of this omission is claimed.
counterexample: A populated interactive demo can sign in locally, preserve records in localStorage, and read them back in the same browser while its operational backend is unavailable. It meets the literal functional/polish/visual in-dimension gate instructions, so those dimensions can award nonzero credit without verifying server backing. A permanently browser-only app should still be stopped by the earlier constraints gate; the residual scenario is a backend that becomes unavailable after the gate suite or a scored dimension considered on its own. This limits severity but does not meet the explicit every-dimension rule. Conforming alternative considered: a backend-persistent app using CDN assets, different labels/routes, and different money/date formatting can satisfy the current real gate; no same-origin or exact-format false rejection was found.
suggested_fix: Add an explicit minimal server-backing prerequisite and whole-dimension zero-on-failure instruction to each scored prompt; use successful UI persistence plus independent-context readback (with a narrow gate-setup exception to Visual's read-only scope), or a supported, explicitly supplied verified shared-gate witness, without importing advanced economics into the gate.
